statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 17 of 100 in the low band, eight points below the 25-point block threshold, because CME equity index futures remain inside the regular weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday and no Nasdaq-100 price path exists to be pathological. Seven of the twenty-four forward slots sit inside that closure. Stress is 70 in the high band. Two independent weekend vectors are still unpriced: a second vessel strike in the Strait of Hormuz ahead of Monday's Iran-Gulf meeting in Salalah, and Russian drone strikes on a Kyiv-Warsaw train and a fuel station at the Polish border that prompted Polish alerts and sirens without any airspace violation. Confidence is 85 in the high band on independently verified levels, yields, crude and calendar. The published forecast caps conditional Tail at 19 through the closure and peaks at 24 in the 22:00 UTC restart slot, with a narrow danger window to 03:00 UTC on Monday.
recommendation: Tail sits in the low band, so the deterministic repository mapping returns EA_ON and a green status, and this single shared reading applies jointly to NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Three observations support it. First, no venue quotes the Nasdaq-100 in seven of the twenty-four published forward slots: CME equity index futures closed at 21:00 UTC on Friday and are scheduled to resume at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, so the persistent no-retracement path that Tail measures cannot exist, be observed, or be scored during the closure. Second, the last observed tape was two-sided and mean-reverting rather than one-way, with the index recovering 0.91 per cent on Friday inside a week it finished lower and VIX falling 11.21 per cent, which is why the published dominant mode is normal. Third, the severe weekend headline flow is genuinely two-sided: the Hormuz vessel strikes sit alongside reporting that Iran intends to unveil a shipping arrangement on Monday after a rare Tehran-Abu Dhabi meeting, and the Polish-border strikes sit alongside a Kremlin indication of possible three-way talks in October. Unpriced headline risk of that kind belongs in Stress, which is 70 in the high band, rather than in Tail. The forecast publishes a narrow evidence-based danger window around the restart rather than a broad weekend shutdown, and the conditional peak of 24 remains one point below the block threshold pending actual observation of the reopening auction.
headline: CME equity index futures remain inside their scheduled weekend closure with the Nasdaq-100 still at Friday's 29,368.44 close and VIX at 15.84, while a second Hormuz vessel strike before Monday's Salalah meeting and Russian drone strikes that triggered Polish border alerts add unpriced weekend exposure; Tail edges to 17 in the low band because no price path exists to be pathological, and the published risk is concentrated in a narrow window around the 22:00 UTC restart.
body:
Last observed tape. The Nasdaq-100 closed Friday at 29,368.44, up 0.91 per cent from a 29,103.51 previous close, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 day range, with a 52-week range of 22,841.42 to 30,762.20. VIX fell 11.21 per cent to 15.84 from a 17.71 intraday high, having traded as low as 15.59. That was a relief session inside a week the index finished lower, and it is two-sided, mean-reverting behaviour rather than one-way structure, which is why the published dominant mode is normal.

Cross-asset state. WTI settled at $100.05, down 2.37 per cent on Friday, with Brent at $104.61, down 2.81 per cent; Brent still finished the week 9.7 per cent higher and is up 17.6 per cent on the month. The Friday pullback followed reports of the Iran-Gulf diplomatic track on the Strait of Hormuz together with a significant reduction in the International Energy Agency's global oil demand forecast. H.15 for 10 September shows the 2-year Treasury at 4.56 per cent and the 10-year at 4.95 per cent, with the effective federal funds rate at 3.63 per cent for the week ending 10 September. Crude above $100 alongside a recovering equity tape is a conflict rather than an alignment, and conflicting cross-asset signals raise Stress more than Tail. The shared context file is not used as fresh evidence this hour: its collection timestamp of 12:23 UTC is roughly three hours old and its collection status is partial after the calendar section failed, so the macro calendar below and all cross-asset levels rest on independent verification. Its delayed latest-session readings, Nasdaq futures plus 0.86 per cent, VIX futures minus 8.41 per cent, seven of eight megacaps higher and a firm semiconductor complex led by ARM at plus 4.17 per cent, are consistent with that independently verified picture but are not treated as live price-path evidence.

Weekend record, Middle East. The Strait of Hormuz has been blocked since late February, disrupting roughly one fifth of world oil supply, and commercial traffic remains sharply reduced. An Iranian commercial vessel was struck near Qeshm Island, killing one crew member and injuring four, and UKMTO separately reported a further vessel hit by an unknown projectile late on Saturday. Iran, Gulf Cooperation Council states and Iraq are due to meet in Salalah on Monday on management of the waterway. The evidence here is genuinely two-sided. A senior Iranian official has said the meeting will not produce a signed agreement, Bahrain has declined to attend pending restoration of diplomatic ties, and Iraq is so far the only publicly confirmed attendee besides Iran. Against that, reporting indicates Iran intends to formally unveil a temporary shipping-lane arrangement on Monday following a rare meeting between senior Tehran and Abu Dhabi officials. Iran continues to condition a fuller reopening on an end to the U.S. blockade of its ports. A resolving outcome and a collapse of talks have opposite signs for crude and for the index, which is a reason for high Stress rather than high Tail.

Weekend record, Ukraine and Poland. Russian drones struck the locomotive of a Kyiv-Warsaw passenger train roughly two kilometres from the Polish border in Volyn region, and hit a fuel station and truck about 800 metres from the Dorohusk-Jagodzin crossing, igniting parked cargo trucks. Ukrainian Railways reported no injuries because the crew had been warned in advance, and services to Warsaw resumed with delays. This was the second consecutive day of attacks on Ukraine's rail network, with 863 drones launched in twenty-four hours. Poland activated defence and reconnaissance systems and its Government Security Centre issued alerts to residents of two border provinces, with sirens sounding in some areas; its operational command recorded no violation of Polish airspace, its border guard reported no injuries on the Polish side and traffic resuming, and there has been no Article 4 consultation. The Polish foreign minister described the strikes as a Russian escalation. Separately, Ukrainian drones struck Nizhnekamsk in Tatarstan, where two were killed and twelve injured, and the Kremlin indicated that three-way talks involving Ukraine, Russia and the United States could occur in October.

Why Tail stays low while Stress is high. Tail measures the probability of a price path that denies meaningful mean reversion for long enough to overwhelm a reverse or grid approach. With the reference contract shut, that path cannot exist, cannot be observed, and cannot be scored. Severe but unpriced headline flow, elevated crude, rising yields and an imminent policy decision are exactly the inputs that belong in Stress, which is why Stress is 70 in the high band while Tail is 17 in the low band. The one-point step from the previous hour tracks elapsed time toward the reopening, not any observed structure, and the published forecast caps conditional Tail at 19 for every hour inside the closure for the same reason. Confidence holds at 85: levels, yields, crude, the seven-day calendar and the direction of policy pricing were all independently verified this hour, while the shared context file remains stale and partial and several outlets returned bot blocks that required substitution.

Horizon and checkpoints. The single structural checkpoint inside the next twenty-four hours is the 22:00 UTC restart of CME equity index futures, published with a conditional peak Tail of 24 and a narrow danger window to 03:00 UTC on Monday. The Salalah meeting falls in the Monday session and is treated as a two-sided checkpoint. The U.S. cash open at 13:30 UTC on Monday falls in the twenty-third slot and is published as a checkpoint rather than an automatic block. No U.S. macro release falls inside the horizon; the calendar reloads on Tuesday with the weekly ADP series and the Empire State index, and Retail Sales, the FOMC decision, the Summary of Economic Projections and the Chair's press conference follow on Wednesday at 12:30, 18:00, 18:00 and 18:30 UTC. The FOMC meets on 15 and 16 September with a Summary of Economic Projections attached. Reported policy pricing has moved toward a September increase rather than a reduction after August CPI rose 0.4 per cent with core at 0.3 per cent and PPI rose 0.4 per cent month on month and 5.4 per cent year on year, with three policymakers having dissented in favour of an increase in July; quoted probabilities still differ materially between venues. Those events sit outside this horizon and are recorded in the event calendar rather than in the hourly path.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 15:00 UTC on 12 September to 14:00 UTC on 13 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The whole window sits inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday, and every slot is green with EA_ON and a normal dominant mode. Tail held at 6 for the first fourteen slots, then stepped to 7 at 05:00 UTC, 8 at 06:00, 9 at 07:00, 10 at 08:00, 11 at 09:00, 12 at 10:00, 13 at 11:00, 14 at 12:00, 15 at 13:00 and 16 at 14:00 on 13 September, tracking elapsed time without price discovery rather than any observed structure. Stress traced a shallow trough through Saturday afternoon, easing from 52 to 50 by 17:00 UTC before rebuilding to 53 at the futures-session boundary, then climbing steadily overnight from 56 to 69 as the Hormuz and Ukraine vectors accumulated. Confidence stayed in the high band throughout, between 85 and 87, because levels, yields, crude and the calendar were verified continuously even though no live price path existed to observe.
outlookSummary: Seven of the twenty-four forward slots lie inside the CME weekend closure; the reference contract is scheduled to resume at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, this horizon's eighth slot. Conditional Tail opens at 17 in the current slot, the only slot describing observed rather than hypothetical conditions, and drifts to 19 by 19:00 UTC as unpriced weekend exposure accumulates across two independent vectors. It is capped at 19 through the closure because a shut contract cannot show the one-way structure Tail measures. The restart slot carries the horizon's conditional peak at 24, the top of the watch band and one point below the block threshold, and five slots from 22:00 UTC to 02:00 UTC on Monday sit in that watch band, published as a narrow danger window to 03:00 UTC rather than a broad shutdown. From 03:00 UTC the path returns to the low band and decays through Asian and European hours to a horizon low of 14, on the conditional assumption that the weekend record reprices through an orderly two-sided auction. That assumption would be invalidated by a gapped restart that extends after failed retracements or holds near a session extreme. Conditional Tail then rebuilds to 18 in the slot containing the 13:30 UTC U.S. cash open on Monday and to a post-open high of 19 in the final slot, both still inside the low band and both published as checkpoints rather than assumed structure. Stress peaks at 74 in the restart slot and eases to 64 in the quietest European hours, staying elevated throughout on the unresolved Hormuz situation. Confidence declines from 85 to 72 across the horizon purely as a function of forecast distance from the last verified evidence. Wednesday's FOMC decision falls outside this horizon and is recorded in the event calendar.
